label: fw.wad, the mod's textures, judged as one set: a concrete wall, a wet concrete floor, a steel grate with holes, a catwalk floor, a pipe-covered wall, a hazard-striped trim, a rusted steel plate, a control panel with dials, a sodium lamp's face (lit), the water, a sign reading PUMP 3, a door

halfLifeDetail.band: T5's band is least to most, Half-Life's own from the 5th to the 95th in 100: fine detail inside it is Valve's own range (a quartile is no bound); under least reads smeared or flat, over most noisy. A texture the brief asks to be one plain colour is flat in Valve's too (its BLACK and YELLOW are 0): flat is right there, and T5 is 2

T1.reason: Thirteen of the fourteen read as what the brief names: fw_concwall and fw_concfloor as concrete, fw_grate as a grate, fw_pipewall with its pipes and elbow, fw_hazard as hazard paint, fw_rustplate as rust, fw_ctrlpanel with dials and switches, fw_lamp as a caged lit sodium face, fw_pump3 legibly reading PUMP 3, fw_door as a panelled door, fw_steel as a bolted plate. fw_water is a flat dark green surface with faint streaks and no ripple or sheen, so it reads as a green panel more than water. fw_concwet is a darker speckle with little sign of wetness, so it only just reads as a wet floor.

T2.reason: Most colours sit in the brief's palette: grey concrete, orange rust, yellow hazard and PUMP 3 sign, orange sodium lamp, green-grey door and water. fw_catwalk is visibly mauve-purple with green patches across all four plates, which breaks the grey-green industrial palette the brief sets. The water is dark green, close to the brief's green-grey.

T3.reason: Seams, plates and bolts sit at believable scale on their faces: fw_concwall's horizontal and vertical seams, fw_catwalk's 2x2 plate grid, fw_steel's bolted panel lines, fw_door's panels and window, fw_pipewall's horizontal runs, fw_grate's 8-pixel cells, fw_hazard's stripe pitch. Sizes are as the brief and the map would expect. Judged by eye at the picture's scale, not measured.

T4.reason: No repeat seam is visible at the edges of the tiles by eye: the walls, floors and plates carry their pattern to every edge without a bright or dark strip. The step across the edges was not measured, so this is by eye only, and the water's vertical streaks are the thing to check first if the step measure is run.

T5.reason: fw_water measures 2.8 detail, below the Half-Life band's floor of 10.8, and it reads flat and smeared in the picture: a plain dark green with barely any fine detail. Every other texture is inside the band (fw_concwall 23.7, fw_concwet 12.9, fw_grate 35.7, fw_catwalk 18.3, fw_pipewall 27, fw_hazard 24.6, fw_rustplate 36.5, fw_ctrlpanel 25.5, fw_lamp 44.1, fw_pump3 36.3, fw_door 18, fw_steel 20.5, fw_concfloor 27.4). The water is not a plain colour the brief asks for, so flat is wrong here.

T6.reason: Every name and size matches the brief's list: 128x128 for fw_concwall, fw_concwet, fw_pipewall, fw_rustplate, fw_concfloor; 64x64 for fw_grate, fw_catwalk, fw_water, fw_steel; 128x32 fw_hazard; 128x64 fw_ctrlpanel; 32x64 fw_lamp; 64x32 fw_pump3; 64x128 fw_door. The '{' grate has holes where the original would, the '!' water is a liquid, and the '~' lamp shows a lit sodium face. No animation was asked for.
